html:
Monks Mound, near the Mississippi River in what is now Illinois, is the largest prehistoric earthen mound in the Americas. It was built in stages from about 900 to 1200 CE at the centre of Cahokia, the greatest city of the Mississippian culture.

The mound rises about 30 metres and covers some 6 hectares at its base, built from millions of baskets of earth carried by hand. A large building, perhaps the house of the paramount chief, stood on its top, facing a great plaza where crowds played the game of chunkey.

At its peak around 1100 Cahokia may have had 10,000 to 20,000 people, larger than London at the time. It was abandoned by about 1350. Its farmers grew maize along with the older native crops, and its builders were heirs of Hopewell mound builders.
